prompt.en: The receive-input meter in digital-mode software clips because the audio interface is overdriven. The incoming RF signal is normal. Which adjustment targets the fault?

text.en: Reduce receiver-audio or interface input level before sampling.

feedback.en: The excessive level is on the receive-audio path before conversion. Reduce it there so peaks fit the sampling range.

text.en: Increase receiver-audio level to fill the converter range more fully.

feedback.en: The peaks already exceed the input range. More audio drive makes clipping worse.

text.en: Reduce computer transmit-playback level before the radio audio input.

feedback.en: Playback is the opposite audio direction. It does not reduce the receive-input level.

text.en: Change push-to-talk timing so the software samples later.

feedback.en: Push-to-talk controls transmit switching, not the amplitude range of receive samples.

explanation.en: Receive and transmit audio are separate directions. Fix clipping before the overloaded receive converter rather than adjusting transmit controls.

prompt.en: A linear regulator has 19 V input, 13.8 V output, and a 3 A load. The exercise heat sink can handle 10 W. Which heat estimate and decision fit?

text.en: 15.6 W; the stated heat sink is too small.

feedback.en: The regulator drops 5.2 V. At 3 A, 5.2 x 3 = 15.6 W becomes heat, above the exercise rating.

text.en: 5.2 W; the stated heat sink has margin.

feedback.en: 5.2 is the voltage drop in volts, not heat in watts. Multiply it by the load current.

text.en: 41.4 W; the stated heat sink is too small.

feedback.en: 13.8 x 3 = 41.4 W is delivered to the load. Regulator heat comes from the voltage dropped across the regulator.

text.en: 57 W; the stated heat sink is too small.

feedback.en: 19 x 3 = 57 W is input power. Subtract the output power, or multiply current by the regulator voltage drop.

explanation.en: Linear-regulator heat is input-output voltage difference times current. Input power and useful load power are different quantities.

prompt.en: A qualified technician has unplugged a linear supply before internal service. Which next plan accounts for stored capacitor energy?

text.en: Use the dark power lamp as the indication that internal work can begin.

feedback.en: The lamp can be off while capacitors remain charged. It is not a stored-voltage measurement.

text.en: Wait for the bleeder resistor, then begin once the case has cooled.

feedback.en: A bleeder may fail, and a cool case does not show capacitor voltage. Controlled discharge and verification are still needed.

text.en: Follow controlled discharge procedures, then verify capacitor voltage with a meter.

feedback.en: Unplugging removes the source, not necessarily stored charge. Qualified service follows the specified discharge procedure and verifies the result.

text.en: Open the interlocked cover and use the open switch as proof of discharge.

feedback.en: An interlock removes a power path. It does not prove stored energy is gone.

explanation.en: Removing input power and removing stored energy are separate safety steps. An indicator or interlock does not replace controlled discharge and verification.
